content.comment_body: Hello everyone, To compare constant values (less than 19999) with an analog value efficiently, you can use a block like an "analog threshold trigger". Below are general techniques for testing an analog value Ax against a constant n (which can be zero): A) To test if Ax equals n: Configure the block parameters as GAIN = 1.0, OFFSET = 0; Threshold ON = n, Threshold OFF = n + 1. For example, if n = 0: ON = 0; OFF = 1. Q output is ON when Ax = 0. B) To check if Ax is greater than n: Set GAIN = 1.0, OFFSET = 0; Threshold ON = OFF = n. If n = 0: ON = 0; OFF = 0. Q output is ON when Ax > 0. This works as a positive number test. C) To check if Ax is less than n: Set GAIN = -1.0, OFFSET = 0; Threshold ON = OFF = -n. For n = 0: GAIN = -1.0; ON = 0; OFF = 0. Q output is ON when Ax < 0. This tests for negative values. D) For Ax >= n: Use GAIN = 1.0, OFFSET = 0; Threshold ON = n, Threshold OFF = n - 1. For n = 2: ON = 2; OFF = 3. Q output is ON when Ax >= 2. E) For Ax <= n: Set GAIN = -1.0, OFFSET = 0; Threshold ON = -n; Threshold OFF = -n - 1. For n = 2: GAIN = -1.0; ON = -2; OFF = -3. Q output is ON when Ax <= 2. With this block, you can also check if an analog value falls inside a range (ON = k1 - 1, OFF = k2, within limits -20000 to 20000). For values or ranges outside this domain, use a "comparator" block in analog mode for direct comparison between two analog values. Guidance for comparing two analog values is available at [url]. Additionally, there is an extended circuit for broader use along with parameter explanations. Please refer to the example circuit "[document]" attached. Best regards, [user_name]
